paper.title_en: Installation and commissioning of pre-production series MuCh-GEM modules in mini-CBM
paper.abstract_en: The Compressed Baryonic Matter (CBM) experiment at the future Facility for Antiproton and Ion Research (FAIR), Darmstadt, Germany, is designed to investigate strongly interacting matter at high baryon densities. The Muon Chamber (MuCh) system of CBM will employ Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) detectors in the first two stations to sustain high interaction rates and particle fluxes. As part of the FAIR Phase-0 program, two large-area trapezoidal triple-GEM detector modules corresponding to MuCh Station-1 and Station-2 were commissioned and tested during the mini-CBM (mCBM) beam campaign at GSI in May 2025. The detectors were operated with high-intensity heavy-ion beams together with other CBM subsystems. Beam tests were performed using <math altimg="si1.svg" display="inline" id="d1e264"><mrow><msup><mrow/><mrow><mn>209</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Bi</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>68</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ions at 1.1-1.7 AGeV incident on Au targets, with beam intensities reaching up to <math altimg="si2.svg" display="inline" id="d1e282"><mrow><mn>8</mn><mo linebreak="goodbreak" linebreakstyle="after">×</mo><mn>1</mn><msup><mrow><mn>0</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>8</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> ions per spill. Detector response, digi rate behaviour, time correlation, spatial correlation, and performance stability were investigated. Preliminary analysis demonstrates stable detector operation, linear response with increasing beam intensity, and good correlation with the Time-of-Flight (TOF) detector. The measured particle flux handling capability reached approximately <math altimg="si3.svg" display="inline" id="d1e299"><mrow><mn>400</mn><mspace class="nbsp" width="0.33em"/><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">kHz/cm</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math> in the highest occupancy regions. These results validate the suitability of the MuCh-GEM detectors for operation in the high-rate CBM environment.
